newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia charges alleged killers of Belgium's Cools.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia charges alleged killers of Belgium's Cools.

text.p: Two Tunisian men suspected of murdering leading Belgian politician Andre Cools in 1991 were charged by a Tunisian magistrate after confessing, a senior judicial official said on Thursday.

Tunisian General Prosecutor Mohamed Lejmi told Reuters the two men, Abdelmajid el-Almi, born in 1965, and Abdeljelil ben Brahim, born in 1973, were charged after they made "important" confessions to the investigating judge on Wednesday.
Official sources said the two suspects confessed during their questioning by police that they had killed Cools in a mafia-style murder.
"They confessed having received a contract killing from an European when they were living in Europe," a source close to the investigation said.
Prosecutor Lejmi said the Tunisian investigating magistrate has issued to his Belgian counterpart in Liege, Belgium, letters aimed at shedding more light on some aspects of the affair.
"The visit to Liege by a Tunisian magistrate might be useful, and even necessary," Lejmi said.
The move was part of a Belgian-Tunisian judicial cooperation prompted by the arrests. It was discussed on Thursday by Tunisian Justice Minister Sadok Chaabane and Belgian Ambassador Daniel Leroy.
Lejmi said that a the time of the crime, the two men were living in Italy and were visiting Belgium from time to time.
"Further investigations are necessary to define to what organisation they belong. A fundamentalist group, among others, must not be excluded," he said.

Investigation sources said that one of the accused, el-Almi, had contacts with a man named Maaroufi, whose name was cited during the trial of a group of fundamentalist arms smugglers last year in Belgium, known as the Zaoui trial.
Belgian teletext said the two men were hired in Sicily with the help of the local mafia.
Lejmi said there is no treaty allowing extradition of the two suspects to Belgium, and that they would be tried in Tunisia.
Cools, a former Socialist minister, was shot at point-blank range in the car park outside his mistress's apartment near the eastern Belgian city of Liege on July 18, 1991.
The ministry said Tunisia normally did not extradite its nationals, which would make it unlikely the two will stand trial in Belgium.
Six people, including former government minister Alain Van der Biest, have been arrested and charged with orchestrating Cools's murder. Van der Biest denies any involvement in the killing.
It is not known who ordered the murder or why, although the crime has been linked to an announcement by Cools that he would make revelations about corruption in the francophone Socialist party.
According to lawyers for some of the accused, witnesses told investigators the murder was a contract killing for 750,000 Belgian francs ($25,000).
Over the past five years the inquiry into Cools's death and his role in the top ranks of the Socialist Party has uncovered corruption at the highest levels of Belgian government.
The scandal has led to the resignation of four ministers and NATO Secretary General Willy Claes and the suicide of a top general.
